newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bonds end lower, money market rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bonds end lower, money market rates fall.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended with a slightly weaker bias but prices of shorter maturities surged after news the Swiss National Bank cut interest rates.
The rate cut was announced as the Swiss Treasury was closing bidding on a new two-tranche bond issue.
"It (the rate cut) was a surprise, and I have a feeling the markets were surprised as well," said Peter Thomann, head of the Swiss Federal Treasury in an interview with Reuters.
The Treasury allocated a large 1.0 billion Swiss francs in the new long tranche of the offering, maturing 2008, which reopens the a 4-1/4 percent January 2008 bond CH108546=.

Thomann said the Treasury could set another issue for payment in the current year if it were necessary. But he also said that the Treasury had nearly met its borrowing goal of five billion Swiss francs gross for the year.
He said the large allocation in the one billion tranche reflected the Treasury's view that yields are currently attractive for borrowers.

A head trader at a Swiss bank said the shorter tranche, which reopened a 5-1/2 percent January 2005 CH322523= bond, was slightly disappointing. He said the bond would probably be used as more of an arbitrage tool between cash and futures.
He said the longer tranche was more attractive and would likely draw some investors out of the April 2006 benchmark, and the June 2007 government bond.

The trader expected bond prices to ease further, with 4.00 percent key resistance for yields in the long end. The SNB rate cut had little impact on the long end. "We saw not one trade after this announcement. It was dead," he said.

Prices in the short end jumped after the announcement, and money market rates also slid. Traders quoted tomorrow/next money midafternoon at roughly 1.00 to 1-3/8 percent compared with 1-5/16 to 1-3/8 percent this morning.
Later in the day Smithkline Beecham Capital Plc set a 125 million Swiss franch issue via Merrill Lynch.
The issue with, a coupon of 3.25 percent matures in November 1996, and was priced at 102.25.
The bond was quoted at less 1.60, less 1.40 on brokers screens, yielding 3.075 percent on less 1.60.

Bond market sources said the new issue is one of the first to be allowed to be listed in Switzerland under a combination of both Swiss and British law. Swiss laws still apply in terms of investor protection but some aspects of the transaction are under British law, sources said.
--- Closing prices as follows:
Dec conf futures CONFZ6 down two at 114.3840
Dec comi medium-term bond COMIZ6 up 20 at 109.95.
Dec Euro Swiss francs FESZ6 up 19 at 98.45.
(Wednesday 103.65/75 yld 4.02 pct)
